short: An emperor's broadcast and a signing in Tokyo Bay ended the Second World War.
full:
Japan's Supreme Council remained divided after Hiroshima, the Soviet declaration of war and Nagasaki. Hirohito broke the deadlock, and on 15 August 1945 a recording of his voice, which almost none of his subjects had heard before, told them that the war situation had developed not necessarily to Japan's advantage. A group of officers had tried to seize the recording the previous night to prevent the broadcast; their coup collapsed within hours.

The formal instrument of surrender was signed on 2 September aboard the battleship Missouri in Tokyo Bay, with MacArthur presiding and representatives of nine Allied nations signing in turn. The occupation of Japan ran until 1952 and produced a new constitution renouncing war as a sovereign right. Six years of fighting had killed somewhere between 60 and 80 million people, the majority of them civilians. The last Japanese holdout, Hiroo Onoda, was persuaded to lay down his arms in the Philippines in 1974.
